title: Enterprise onboarding + escalation + QBR & health checks playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's enterprise onboarding steps, escalation procedures, integration guidelines, known issues & workarounds, and the standard QBR / health-check materials used by Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), and Support. It is intended to be a single reference for onboarding new platform customers and for operationalizing escalations and recurring health reviews.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Covers onboarding from kickoff through go-live and first 90 days, the support escalation flow (Severity 1-4), high-level integration guidance for common customer topologies, curated known issues and mitigations, and QBR/health-check templates.
- Audience: CSMs, SEs, Support Engineers, SRE on-call, and customer technical stakeholders.

Phases of enterprise onboarding (high level):
1) Pre-kickoff (CSM + Sales)
   - Confirm contract terms (capacity, Dedicated/Private options, SLAs).
   - Collect customer inventory: network topology, VPC peering, KMS/HSM needs, data residency, and compliance constraints.
   - Assign roles: Primary CSM, Technical Lead (customer), SE, and Primary Support Engineer.

2) Kickoff (Week 0)
   - Deliverables: Project plan, success criteria, contact matrix, and sandbox credentials (if applicable).
   - Agenda template: introductions, scope, timelines, integration overview, security & compliance review.

3) Integration & validation (Weeks 1-4)
   - Network setup: VPC rules, CIDR ranges, firewall rules - reference network checklist below.
   - Authentication: API keys for Hosted, or org-level cert/KMS integration for Dedicated/Private.
   - Test plan: sample requests, perf/latency baselines, end-to-end functional tests (generation, embeddings, streaming).
   - Acceptance criteria: Successful end-to-end tests, ability to authenticate from customer infra, and observed latency < agreed SLO during baseline load.

4) Pilot & ramp (Weeks 4-12)
   - Pilot targets: A small percentage of production traffic; validate autoscaling and batching behavior.
   - Monitoring: enable per-route telemetry, cost attribution, and request/response sampling.
   - Rollout policy: Canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback triggers defined.

5) Go-live & handoff (post-pilot)
   - Handoff doc: final runbook, alerting thresholds, SLOs, on-call contacts, and scheduled QBR cadence.
   - Knowledge transfer session between SE and customer operations.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): project plan, stakeholder coordination, contract compliance, QBR facilitation.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): network validation, authentication, integration verification, test plan ownership.
- Support Engineer / Escalation Lead: first responder for P1/P2 incidents, triage, and liaison to Eng/SRE.
- SRE/Runtime Engineering: model-serving incidents, capacity/throughput issues, kernel/runtime fixes.
- Customer Technical Lead: provides access, test data, and operational readiness.

Network & security pre-check checklist (table represented as bullet list):
- Required: Allowed egress to api.redwood.ai (hosted) or IP ranges (dedicated/private) - provide specific CIDR list to customer.
- Ports: TLS (443) outbound; for Private deployments refer to on-prem reference-architecture docs for port matrix.
- KMS/HSM: confirm algorithm support (AES-GCM, RSA), key rotation policy, and key access roles.
- TLS certs: plan for mutual TLS for Private deployments if requested.

Integration guide (common topologies):
1) Hosted API (typical SaaS integration):
   - Steps: Provision API key -> Configure client timeout/retry policy -> Run functional smoke tests (generation, embedding) -> Enable streaming if needed.
   - Common issues: API key mis-scopes, excessive client timeouts leading to dropped streaming connections.
   - Example curl smoke test:
     curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

2) Dedicated / Private (customer-managed network):
   - Steps: Exchange IP ranges and certificates -> Configure routing and firewall rules -> KMS/HSM integration -> Install customer agent (if on-prem) -> Run performance baseline.
   - Validation items: KV cache warmup, batch sizing behavior, latency under target load.

Support process and SLAs (triage & response):
- Severity definitions and target response times (CS-owned):
  - S1 (P1) - Production outage (no reads/writes): Initial acknowledgement 15 min, engineering triage 60 min, mitigation or rollback within 2 hours or ongoing updates every 30 min.
  - S2 (P2) - Partial outage or severe degradation: Initial acknowledgement 30 min, triage 2 hours, fix/mitigation within 24 hours (or agreed timeline).
  - S3 (P3) - Functional bug with workaround: Acknowledgement within 4 business hours, resolution per normal backlog.
  - S4 (P4) - Feature request or minor issue: Standard support channel.
- Escalation path:
  1) Customer opens ticket via support portal or email to support@redwood (CSM copied for enterprise accounts).
  2) Support Engineer performs initial triage, documents logs and reproducible steps.
  3) If unresolved at Tier 1/Tier 2 within SLA, escalate to Escalation Lead and SE.
  4) For runtime or capacity incidents, Escalation Lead engages SRE and Runtime Eng with runbook link and correlation IDs.
  5) Exec notification for incidents meeting business-impact thresholds (ex: >3 customers impacted or >4 hours downtime for a single enterprise).

Escalation matrix (contacts - roles only):
- Tier 1 Support: Support Engineer on primary queue (CSM notified)
- Tier 2 Escalation: Escalation Lead (Support manager)
- Technical escalation: SE / Runtime Eng (eng-serving-runtime)
- Capacity / infra: SRE on-call
- Executive/Customer success exec escalation: CSM Director

Runbook pointers to include in an escalation ticket:
- Title, Severity, Customer, Correlation IDs, Recent request IDs, Topology (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), Steps already taken, Attach: sanitized logs, timeline, and observed metrics (latency percentiles, error-rate, token throughput).

Known issues & workarounds (curated list):
- Issue: Intermittent 502s for streaming responses on older HTTP client libs
  - Symptom: Streaming connections close mid-response, status 502 returned intermittently.
  - Workaround: Upgrade HTTP client to support chunked transfer; retry on idempotent requests; configure keepalive to 60s.
  - Owner: eng-developer-experience / support

- Issue: Elevated tail latency during cold KV cache for long context sequences
  - Symptom: P99 latency spikes when requests reference long prefix history after idle period.
  - Workaround: Pre-warm KV cache with short priming requests or use a warmed baseline traffic generator during business hours.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime

- Issue: Private deployment TLS mismatch after cert rotation
  - Symptom: Connections fail with TLS handshake errors post-rotation.
  - Workaround: Ensure rotation includes both ingress and agent certs; coordinate clock drift and intermediate CA updates.
  - Owner: eng-private-deployments

- Issue: Token accounting drift vs customer analytics (small discrepancies)
  - Symptom: Customer reports token consumption higher than expected for certain routes.
  - Workaround: Investigate prompt truncation/encoding differences; provide route-level token reports and encourage use of server-side rate limiting and batching.
  - Owner: finance-and-legal (billing ops) + eng-platform

Operational playbook snippets (procedural):
1) P1 incident quick checklist:
   - Acknowledge & declare incident in status page system.
   - Assemble war room (CSM, SE, Escalation Lead, SRE).
   - Collect correlation IDs and recent request payloads.
   - Rollback last known deploy if suspected cause is release (coordinate with Eng release lead).
   - Communicate every 30 minutes until mitigation.

2) Post-incident postmortem template (required for P1/P2 affecting customers):
   - Summary, timeline, root cause, contributing factors, corrective actions, owners, and follow-up verification plan.

Health checks and QBR materials:
- Quarterly QBR agenda (60-90m):
  1) Executive summary: uptime, major incidents, feature highlights (10m)
  2) Usage & cost trends: tokens, embeddings, average request size, cost-per-request (15m)
  3) Performance & reliability: latency percentiles, error rates, SLO compliance (15m)
  4) Integration health: auth, routing, caching, model-change impacts (10m)
  5) Roadmap & asks: product roadmap items relevant to customer, requested features (10m)
  6) Action items & next steps (10m)
- Standard QBR metrics to collect (minimum):
  - Uptime (30/90/365 day), P99/P95 latency, error rate per route, token consumption (monthly), cost by route, number of incidents (by severity).
  - Business KPIs (customer-provided): model accuracy, user engagement, retention impact.

QBR data sources & dashboards:
- Redwood Console: per-route dashboards, token-level costs, trace sampling.
- Customer-provided analytics: integration for ingestion logs and business KPIs.
- Shared QBR pack: PDF + slide template (CSM to populate prior to QBR).

Templates (checklist snippets to copy):
- Pre-kickoff data collection: customer name; business contact; technical contact; VPC/CIDR; preferred rollout cadence; compliance needs; preferred SLOs.
- Go-live signoff: acceptance test results; runbook delivered; monitoring connected; post-go-live support window scheduled.

Maintenance & cadence:
- Weekly check-ins during ramp (first 4 weeks).
- Bi-weekly during stabilization (weeks 4-12).
- Quarterly QBR after stabilization.

Appendix: links to internal runbooks and reference guides:
- Network & VPC checklist (internal runbook) - link: /confluence/eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking/network-vpc-checklist
- Private deployment reference architecture - link: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures/private-deployment-arch
- Runtime incident runbook - link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-incident-runbook

If you are the CSM preparing an onboarding packet for a customer, copy the pre-kickoff checklist and the kickoff agenda into the customer-facing packet, and schedule the first-week integration validation session with SE and Support present.
